basic_info: 38-year-old male presenting with back pain and pins and needles in the right foot following raking leaves. Partner notes increased pain when standing.
present_illness: Onset of back pain after raking leaves, associated with pins and needles in the right foot. Pain worsens when standing and bending over, but feels better when sitting or taking a hot shower. The pain is described as a tightening feeling in the back, constant since onset, with no radiation beyond the back. Pins and needles in the right foot are present, with no numbness, weakness, or bowel/bladder dysfunction. The back pain is located in the lower back, near the middle of the spine, and does not radiate to other parts of the body. The patient did not notice any changes in posture or gait but was observed by their partner to be standing differently.
past_history: No history of back pain, neurological symptoms in lower extremities, back surgery, trauma, diabetes, or spinal stenosis. This is the first time experiencing such an issue.
physical_exam: Physical examination findings are pending. The patient reported tingling in the right foot and increased pain when standing. A neurological examination has not been performed yet.
aux_exam: An X-ray of the spine was performed and reported as normal. No MRI or CT scan has been performed yet.
